title: Design for error, don’t blame the user
principle: Norman’s public DOET theme (Human Error? No, Bad Design): treat slips and mistakes as design problems—constraints, undo, sensible defaults, clear confirmations. AI flows that only show the success path are incomplete.
procedure: Enumerate likely slips (wrong click, mode errors) and mistakes (wrong goal).
Add forcing functions / constraints where cost of error is high.
Prefer undo over scary confirmations for reversible actions.
Write error copy that explains cause + next step, not blame.
Test the unhappy path in critic screenshots.
examplePrompts:
Add design-for-error (Norman / DOET public principles) to this flow:
- List slips vs mistakes.
- Reversible actions get undo; irreversible get plain-language confirm.
- Error messages: cause + recovery.
- Remove blame language (‘invalid user’).
Return changes.
Replace this ‘Are you sure?’ wall with undo toast where the delete is reversible.
promptWhy: Splits slips/mistakes so fixes match the error type.
Undo vs confirm is an explicit policy models blur.
tips: jnd.org DOET chapter outline covers Designing for Error.
No endorsement; paraphrase public principles only.
